audit_method.coverage: All 92 entire supplied passage text fields were examined against the label-free findings, with an explicit per-candidate audit disposition. Prior reasoning/labels were then checked for consistency; previous model labels were not treated as clinical evidence.
audit_method.scope: Only the complete stored passage text was used; missing sentences or antecedents were not reconstructed from titles, adjacent chunks, external sources or a guessed diagnosis.

rubric.relevant: Direct, substantive information for interpreting a recorded finding or a coherent differential category, including symptom patterns, mechanisms or diagnostic distinctions. It need not explain every finding or describe a likely diagnosis.
rubric.partially_relevant: Some useful but limited information: indirect risk/management context, an isolated nonspecific symptom comparison, or applicability contingent on missing clinical/developmental context.
rubric.not_relevant: No substantive interpretive connection in the supplied text; merely generic word overlap, a different anatomical/contextual pattern, or an unsupported life-stage-specific setting is insufficient.
rubric.uncertain: The available passage is too ambiguous or context-deficient to choose a relevance label confidently. This is not a synonym for diagnostic uncertainty.

clarifications: Relevance is not disease probability. Directly useful symptom characterization can remain relevant despite pediatric rarity; age-specific epidemiology or treatment must not be transferred to this child.
A passage can be relevant to one observed finding; explaining the whole episode is not required. Isolated nonspecific overlap remains partial, not automatically relevant.
A truncated passage can be partially relevant if a definition or warning-sign relation survives. Retain uncertain when the missing subject/relation is necessary to interpret the overlapping words.
A typical location or an optional associated symptom is not a mandatory diagnostic criterion. Explicitly absent radiation is preserved; unknown features remain unknown.

Subjective palpitations are not documented tachycardia, dyspnea is not measured tachypnea, sweating is not automatically nocturnal, and numeric timing/pain values are not converted to unsupported clinical thresholds.
Fear of dying is not suicidal intent, detachment is not psychosis, head trauma is not automatically psychological trauma, and panic-like symptoms are not proof of recurrent panic disorder.
audit_method.confidence_meaning: Confidence in the recommended relevance label, not diagnosis, disease probability or treatment indication. The seven revised labels have medium confidence and remain proposals.

changes.passage_description: Breast pain and local breast warning signs
changes.why_change: The original label discounted directly applicable local symptom information mainly because cancer is unusual at this age. The benchmark asks about useful information for one or more findings, not the probability of the named disease. The same local symptom content is treated as relevant in the general breast-disease passage.
supporting_passage_excerpts: Pain in any area of the breast.
A new lump or thickening in or near the breast or in the armpit.

expected_before.reasoning: The passage explicitly includes breast pain and describes local breast and nipple changes that could help characterize the recorded right-breast pain. It does not establish malignancy, and its cancer-specific context has limited applicability to a 10-year-old without recorded breast examination findings.
expected_before.medical_interpretation_notes: Local breast pain is a real overlap, but cancer-specific framing has very limited pediatric applicability and no local examination is supplied.

set.reasoning: The passage explicitly discusses pain in any area of the breast and accompanying breast/nipple changes, providing direct information for interpreting the recorded right-breast pain. The examination findings are unknown, and the cancer-specific framing must not be treated as evidence that a 10-year-old has malignancy. Its local symptom-assessment content remains relevant independently of cancer likelihood.
set.medical_interpretation_notes: Distinguish useful local breast symptom characterization from the very different question of pediatric cancer probability.

changes.passage_description: Diverticular abdominal cramping and pain pattern
changes.why_change: The original rationale treated the typical lower-abdominal site as an exclusive location and overlooked the broader abdominal-pain and onset information. expected_before.reasoning: The clinical focus is lower-abdominal, especially left-lower-abdominal, pain with bowel changes or fever. The documented pain is in the chest, breast, flank and hypochondria, not the lower abdomen. The word cramping alone provides little useful interpretation of that distribution or the associated respiratory and sensory symptoms.

set.reasoning: The passage supplies limited gastrointestinal comparison for the recorded abdominal/hypochondrial cramping: it discusses abdominal pain, cramping, onset and associated bowel or fever symptoms. Its typical lower-left distribution does not match the documented upper-abdominal/flank locations well, but 'most often' does not restrict every presentation to that site. Bowel changes, chronicity and fever remain unknown; no diverticular diagnosis is inferred.
set.medical_interpretation_notes: Typical lower-left pain differs from the observed upper-abdominal/flank pain, but the text does not make the typical location obligatory; this is a borderline partial/not-relevant decision.
